name: Soft tape/analog saturation on pads before space FX
goal: Make digital/synth pads and string layers feel denser and less sterile by adding gentle tape or analog-style saturation early (before big reverb/space): zero-time tape-delay as low-CPU tape sat, or gentle console/tape emulations kept near 0 VU—fullness in low-mids without obvious distortion.

source.title: How to mix Pads & Strings - The complete process - Part 1 - Saturation - Mini Series

prerequisites: Pad/string/synth sustain layer; tape sat, tape delay, or gentle analog-drive plugin/module

inputs.name: drive_level
inputs.description: Keep near unity/0 VU for gentle sat; only push for intentional grit

outputs.name: saturated_pad_bus
outputs.description: Pad/string bus with soft sat ahead of later FX

steps.action: Identify sterile/digital pad or synth-string sustains that need density. Goal is subtle analog juice, not crunch.
steps.expect: Target layer sounds clean/digital and thin in low-mids

steps.action: Option A — low-CPU tape: insert a tape-delay emulator, set delay time to zero so only tape saturation remains (no echoes).
steps.expect: Subtle fullness/compression in low-mids without audible delay

steps.action: Option B — gentle console/tape emulation: raise input until meters approach ~0 (not deep into red) for natural saturation; back off if obvious distortion appears.
steps.expect: Analog-ish body; needles near zero, not hard clipping

steps.action: A/B dry vs sat: expect slightly fuller low-mid presence and mild soft compression—rewind/listen carefully; changes are subtle by design.
steps.expect: Pad feels more real/dense, not crushed

steps.action: Then continue the pad chain (EQ/chorus/delay/reverb). Keep this sat stage before big space so reverb blooms on the denser tone.
steps.expect: Saturation precedes space FX in the rack

verification: Saturation is gentle (near 0 VU / no obvious crunch unless intended)
Pad low-mids feel fuller vs dry
No unintended delay tails from zero-time tape-delay trick
